name: Osaka
description: Umeda to Shinsekai along Midosuji, with Osaka Castle, from open data: every building height is a Project PLATEAU measurement, lit by the real sun.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, compatible with CC BY 4.0)

level.name: Osaka Castle's honmaru round the keep
level.note: DEM5A interpolates a false terrace up to 40.5 m east of the keep, where the laser points were filtered out with the keep and its stone base. The 10 m DEM reads 31.5 to 32.6 m there and PLATEAU puts the ground under the keep at 30.9 to 31.7 m, so the honmaru is levelled to 31.2 m, DEM5A's median over the open plaza just south of it.

level.name: Ebisubashi's north head
level.note: The DEM keeps the old bridge's approach as a hump across Ebisubashi-suji that stands up to 0.2 m over the drawn bridge's end (cities/osaka/city.py, EBISU) and falls 0.6 m across the street. The street at the bridge's north end, from 5 m on the bridge to 6 m past it and 10 m either side of its line, is levelled to the end of its deck, 3.9 m (the street's line in OpenStreetMap is at 3.9 m there).

level.name: Ebisubashi's south head
level.note: The same at the south end, under the Glico sign: levelled to the end of the deck, 4.1 m (the street's line, 4.1 to 4.2 m).

terrain.attribution: GSI DEM5A, 5 m bare earth from airborne laser survey, with the 10 m DEM where it has gaps (GSI terms of use, compatible with CC BY 4.0)

plateau.attribution: Project PLATEAU, Osaka City 3D city model 2020 (MLIT; CityGML v2; building survey 2017), PLATEAU site policy (compatible with CC BY 4.0)

seawall.note: The rivers' concrete revetments (gogan) under a concrete coping.

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from the cities' street-tree surveys and the parks' own guides: ginkgo and zelkova (keyaki) are Japan's commonest street trees, with plane trees and camphor; the woods are the laurel forest's evergreen broadleaves and camphors, with zelkovas, black pines, maples and a few cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too). Areas give the parks and precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own; their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py). Somei-yoshino cherries (sakura) line Tokyo's streets after the ginkgo and the zelkova, and stand in the parks' lawns and along the rivers and moats; areas give the places known for them a mix of their own.

areas.name: Japan Mint
areas.note: The Mint's riverside passage, open a week each April under some 340 cherries of 140 kinds.

areas.name: Kema Sakuranomiya Park
areas.note: Some 4,800 cherries along the Okawa's east bank (Osaka City); its outline is the riverside path, widened.

areas.name: Midosuji
areas.note: Midosuji is lined with ginkgos its whole 4 km (Osaka City), gold in late November, bare by late December.

tour.title: Osaka from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from Project PLATEAU, OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps, on GSI's 5 m laser terrain under GSI aerial photos, from Umeda in the north to Shinsekai in the south.

tour.title: Osaka Castle
tour.text: The keep stands on a 13.3 m stone base and rises 39.4 m above it: five roofs outside, eight floors inside. Each tier's plan, its eaves and its gables are measured from PLATEAU's 3D model of the keep. The small keep platform in front carries the Kinmeisui well house of 1626.

tour.title: Nakanoshima, the island in the river
tour.text: Between the Dojima and Tosabori rivers: the Central Public Hall in red brick, the City Hall, and the Festival Towers at 199 m. The rivers are water in the model, so boats can sail them.

tour.title: Umeda
tour.text: Osaka Station, the Umeda Sky Building at 173 m and the red wheel of HEP FIVE, 106 m above the street. Several of these towers are newer than PLATEAU's 2017 survey, so their heights come from OpenStreetMap.

tour.title: Dotonbori at dusk
tour.text: The Glico runner, the Kani Doraku crab and the canal that Yasui Doton began digging in 1612. The sign and the crab are indicative models placed by their published positions.

tour.title: Namba Parks
tour.text: The Jerde Partnership's mall on the site of the old Osaka Stadium, opened in 2003: a canyon curves through it, and its roof is a park, terraces stepping up from the 2nd floor by Nankai Namba station to the 9th.

tour.title: Tsutenkaku
tour.text: The tower of Shinsekai: {landmark:tsutenkaku.published_m} m, {landmark:tsutenkaku.with_rod_m} m with the lightning rod, rebuilt in 1956. The gold observatory is on the fifth floor at {landmark:tsutenkaku.observatory_m} m.

tour.title: Midosuji
tour.text: Opened in 1937: 44 m wide and 4 km long, from Umeda in the north to Namba, lined with ginkgo all the way. All of its traffic runs south, one way, as it has since 1970.

tour.title: Winter sun in Utsubo Park
tour.text: The study asks how much of each park stays in direct sun between 8:00 and 16:00 on the winter solstice. Utsubo Park, boxed in by towers, gets {sun:靱公園|12-21|12:00}% of its area at noon.

reference_heights.source: Wikipedia, List of tallest buildings in Osaka (October 2026), architectural heights; heights are as published, so spires and rooftop plant count

protection.title: Winter-solstice sun study (a study rule, not Osaka law)
protection.summary: Japan's shadow rule (日影規制, Building Standards Act art. 56-2) limits the hours of winter-solstice shade a new building may cast on neighbouring land between 8:00 and 16:00, but only in the zones a local authority lists, and, as we read it, not in commercial zones, which is most of this model. Osaka's parks have no such rule, so this study applies the same date and window to them as a test, not as law.
protection.source_note: The 8:00 to 16:00 window and the exclusion of commercial zones are our reading of the Act and secondary sources; check the text before relying on them. The choice of parks and the use of the window for them is this project's own.
protection.reading_note: Japan has no daylight saving, so clock time and standard time are the same here. The baseline is today's model, not the buildings of a fixed date.
protection.tip: Tip: try the blocks beside Utsubo Park, or south of Osaka Castle Park.

sources.landmarks: Osaka Castle keep (Osaka Prefecture fact sheet; Bunshun; tier plans, eaves and gables from PLATEAU's 2025 LOD2 model of the keep, 27100-bldg-328870), the small keep platform and the Kinmeisui well house (PLATEAU 2025), Tsutenkaku (Osaka City leaflet; observatory and deck heights from tourist sources), HEP FIVE wheel: published dimensions; the Glico sign and Kani Doraku crab are indicative

weather.source: Osaka: Japan Meteorological Agency, 1991-2020 normals, days with at least 0.5 mm

game.title: Osaka on Foot

ferry_style.note: The shared river shuttle, a little shorter, stands in for the Tombori cruise boats and the Aqua Liner; the white and blue are approximate.

game.ferry_note: Landings are the ferry terminals mapped in OpenStreetMap (via Overture). Routes are generated through open water, and the stops follow the Tombori River Cruise and the Aqua Liner, but the timetable and the vessel names are invented. Boats run at 1.5 times real speed (9 m/s) and wait 20 s at each landing. At a landing you can skip the wait.
smalltalk: Meccha ee tenki ya naa. Lovely weather, isn't it?

npcs.name: Mei
idle: Dotonbori is a canal that Yasui Doton began digging in 1612. Everything on its banks is newer than the water.
Come back after dark. The Glico runner lights up over the canal, and the whole street with him.

npcs.name: Daisuke
idle: Maido! Eight to a tray. Mind the heat, the inside is lava.
Flip it fast, flip it again. The octopus is just the excuse; it's the batter that matters.

npcs.name: Kuidaore Taro
idle: Kuidaore! Eat until you drop. In Kyoto they dress until they drop. In Osaka we eat.
Bon bon, bon bon. I drum while you decide between the crab and the takoyaki. Decide quickly.

npcs.name: Kenta
idle: Rokko oroshi ni sassoto! Hanshin Tigers, 2023 Japan Series champions. Thirty-eight years we waited.
Back in 1985 the fans threw a Colonel Sanders statue off this bridge. They found him again in 2009. Don't throw anything off this bridge.

npcs.name: Officer Sato
idle: Lost? The koban on this corner has handed back more umbrellas than you've had lunches.
On the escalators in Osaka we stand on the right and walk on the left. In Tokyo it is the other way round. People get very serious about it.

npcs.name: Fumi
idle: Maido, maido! Ame-chan? Take two. We give candy to strangers here. It's how we say hello.
Mokarimakka? That's how merchants here greet each other: are you making money? The answer is always 'bochi bochi', so-so.

npcs.name: Taisho Kenji
idle: Nidozuke kinshi! No double-dipping in the sauce. There's a cabbage on the table for the scooping. Use it.
Pork, shrimp, lotus root, quail egg. Everything on a stick, everything in the fryer. Shinsekai has always been like this.

npcs.name: Yoshi & Taka
idle: Yoshi: We are the best manzai duo in Namba. Taka: Who said that? Yoshi: My mother. Taka: Nandeyanen!
Taka: Why is the tower so tall? Yoshi: So I can see you from far away. Taka: Nandeyanen!

npcs.name: Tanaka
idle: Ohayo gozaimasu. I take Midosuji every morning: five stops from Umeda to Namba, and I have never once been late.
The underground at Umeda is a dungeon. I've lived here forty years and I still ask the staff for directions.

npcs.name: Captain Nishida
idle: Osaka is called the City of Water. The rivers and canals were the roads here long before the trains.
They used to say Osaka had 808 bridges, hachihyaku-ya-bashi. It's a figure of speech, but I've stopped counting under the first twenty.

npcs.name: Ichiro
idle: Hideyoshi began this castle in 1583. The keep you see is from 1931, built with donations from the people of Osaka. It's concrete under the copper.
From the foot of the stone base to the top of the shachi the keep is {landmark:castle.height_m} m. There's a lift inside, but the stairs are better.

npcs.name: Ryo
idle: This was the Naniwa Palace in the seventh century. The only thing flying here now is me.
Space to climb, C to descend. Don't land on the Sky Building. They get upset.

quests.title: Welcome to Dotonbori
talk: Okaeri! Well, welcome. I'm Mei; I grew up over a shop in Namba. This is Dotonbori, the canal Yasui Doton began digging in 1612.
Look up at the Glico runner, then find Daisuke on the Dotonbori street. He's the one with the headband. He has opinions about octopus.
The Tombori River Cruise leaves from the Taizaemon-bashi landing just along the canal, the helicopter waits on the open lot a block north-east, and a hand up at the kerb (Y) stops a taxi.

steps.text: Find Daisuke, the takoyaki master, on the Dotonbori street

quests.title: Eat until you drop
talk: Maido! Takoyaki: flour batter, a piece of octopus, tenkasu, red ginger, and you turn it with a pick, quick, quick. They say Tomekichi Endo started it in 1935, not far from here.
We have a word for this city: kuidaore. Eat until you drop. In Kyoto they say they dress until they drop.
Take the Tombori River Cruise from Taizaemon-bashi to Nipponbashi. The canal looks different from the water. Then find Fumi at the Kuromon Market and tell her Daisuke sent you.

steps.text: Ride the Tombori River Cruise from Taizaemon-bashi to Nipponbashi
Find Fumi in the Kuromon Market

quests.title: Osaka's kitchen
talk: Maido, maido! Daisuke sent you? Ame-chan, take two. That's how we say hello.
They call this market Osaka's kitchen: fish, fruit, fugu and beef, and the chefs of Namba shop here before dawn. Eat as you walk, everybody does.
Then go and eat kushikatsu in Shinsekai. Kenji is the best.

steps.text: Find Kenji, the kushikatsu chef, in Shinsekai

quests.title: Under the tower
talk: Nidozuke kinshi! One dip only. Good. Eat.
That's Tsutenkaku above you. The first tower came down in 1943; this one went up in 1956. {landmark:tsutenkaku.published_m} m, or {landmark:tsutenkaku.with_rod_m} m with the lightning rod.
The lights at the top tell tomorrow's weather: white for fair, orange for cloudy, blue for rain. Now go to Namba and find the two guys outside the Grand Kagetsu theatre. They'll tell you the rest.

steps.text: Find the manzai comedians near Namba Grand Kagetsu

quests.title: Nandeyanen!
talk: Yoshi: Tsutenkaku is a hundred and three metres. Taka: Nandeyanen! It's a hundred and eight! Yoshi: With the lightning rod. Taka: ...fine.
Taka: Seriously, your Mr Tanaka is waiting at Yodoyabashi. Middle of Midosuji. Takes the subway every day. Yoshi: He has never laughed once. Taka: Get him to laugh. Nandeyanen!

steps.text: Find Mr Tanaka at Yodoyabashi on Midosuji

quests.title: A place in the winter sun
talk: Ohayo gozaimasu. Midosuji: the boulevard from Umeda to Namba, one-way, gingko trees on both sides. In the evening in December they light them. You should see it.
Stand on the right on the escalators here. In Tokyo it's the left. We are not Tokyo.

Utsubo Park, west of here, is boxed in by towers. On 21 December at noon only {sun:靱公園|12-21|12:00}% of the park is in direct sun. Go and stand in it at midday on the winter solstice. Then take the Aqua Liner: Captain Nishida is at Hachikenyahama.

steps.text: Stand in direct sun in Utsubo Park, 10:00 to 14:00 on 21 December

quests.title: The City of Water
talk: Welcome aboard, or nearly. Osaka is the City of Water: the rivers and canals were the roads here long before the trains.
Take the Aqua Liner from Hachikenyahama to Osaka-jo Port. Ichiro is waiting at the keep. Mind the bridges.

steps.text: Ride the Aqua Liner from Hachikenyahama to Osaka-jo Port
Climb up to the keep and find Ichiro

quests.title: The keep
talk: Hideyoshi began this castle in 1583. The keep you see is from 1931, paid for by the people of Osaka. Concrete and steel under the copper.
It stands on a stone base 13.3 m high and rises 39.4 m above it: five roofs outside, eight floors inside. Look for the gilded tigers on the top tier, and the golden shachi on the ridge.
Now go to Naniwa-no-miya Park. Ryo's helicopter is waiting there.

steps.text: Walk to Naniwa-no-miya Park and find Ryo

quests.title: Umeda from the air
talk: Ryo here. Hop in. The helicopter's on the pad.
Fly to Umeda and set down in Umekita Park, the new park beside the station. It's three kilometres north-west. Stay clear of the towers. The Umeda Sky Building alone is 173 m. Don't hit it.
Space to climb, C to descend, W and S for forward and back, A and D to turn. V switches to a bird's-eye view. E gets you out once you've landed.

steps.place: うめきた公園 サウスパーク

steps.text: Report back to Mei at Ebisu-bashi

quests.title: Kuidaore
talk: That's all of it: the canal, the market, the tower, the river, the keep and the air.
And you ate. That's the most Osaka thing of all.
The city is yours. Change the time of day, take any boat, or fly anywhere. Go and see the Glico sign at night.

game.blurb: Walk Dotonbori, Kuromon and Shinsekai, take the Tombori River Cruise and the Aqua Liner, climb to the keep of Osaka Castle and fly over Umeda. Talk to the people who know the city.

storey_note: Calibrated on Project PLATEAU: 118,782 non-residential and 11,163 residential buildings with a storey count and a measured height have a median of 3.4 m and 3.6 m a floor, with no constant term.
